title: 8. Vacancy in the Office of President

blocks.content: When the vacancy occurs in the office of the President due to resignation, removal, death or otherwise, the Vice-President acts as the President until a new President is elected.

rows: Must be held before the expiration of the five-year term
Must be held within 6 months from the date of vacancy
Outgoing President continues in office until successor enters
Vice-President acts as President until new President is elected
Full term of 5 years (not remaining period)

items: The Vice-President can act as President for a maximum period of six months, within which a fresh presidential election must be conducted.
In 1969, Chief Justice M. Hidayatullah acted as President of India when President Dr. Zakir Hussain died and Vice-President V.V. Giri resigned.
When acting as President or discharging President's functions, the Vice-President or CJI enjoys all powers, immunities, and emoluments of the President.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A vacancy in the President's office can occur due to expiration of tenure, resignation, removal by impeachment, death, or setting aside of election by the Supreme Court.
If the vacancy is caused by expiration of tenure, the election to fill the vacancy must be completed before the expiration of the term.
When the vacancy arises due to death, resignation, or removal, an election must be held within six months from the date of occurrence of such vacancy.
The Vice-President acts as President when a vacancy occurs due to death, resignation, or removal until a new President is elected.
If the office of Vice-President is also vacant, the Chief Justice of India (or the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court) discharges the functions of the President.
